tone_patterns: Formal, standards-aligned tone that prioritizes precision and neutrality over promotional language
Assurance-like phrasing emphasizing completeness, neutrality, accuracy, and absence of material error
Reader-guidance tone that instructs how to interpret the disclosures (e.g., how to read alongside other reports)
Cautious, risk-aware language when discussing sensitive information and forward-looking judgements
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short scope statement defining the reporting period and overarching quality characteristics
Uses a bulleted list to enumerate reporting principles/aims, each bullet describing one quality attribute or preparation practice
Transitions from preparation principles to a brief primer on the relevant standards and their purpose
Includes a compliance/adoption statement describing alignment with the standards and the rationale for doing so
Provides a structured explanation of how the standards map to core disclosure pillars (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics/targets)
Adds a contextual paragraph explaining implementation maturity (e.g., first-time adoption) and integration approach
Defines report composition and boundary (what entities/activities are included) and directs readers to related disclosures elsewhere
Uses short sub-sections to address specific general requirements (connected information, comparatives, timing/location, reporting entity/value chain, sources of guidance)
Includes an explicit note on use of prior-period contextual information and how it is flagged within the report
heading_patterns: Section opener uses a large numeric index paired with a short title (e.g., '01' + section name) as a visual chapter marker
Repeats the section title at the top of subsequent pages as a running header for navigation
Subsections are numbered hierarchically (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3) with descriptive titles aligned to IFRS S1/S2 general requirement topics
Subsection headings appear as standalone lines with clear spacing before body text to support scanability
table_patterns: No tables used in the excerpt; content relies on bullets and narrative for general requirements
Where cross-references are needed, the pattern is to cite notes/appendices in text rather than embedding a table
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No figures/diagrams used in the excerpt; emphasis is on structured narrative and bullet lists
pdf_layout_patterns: Chapter divider page with prominent section number and title, minimal additional text
Running header on content pages repeating the section title for orientation
Footer includes page number and report title for consistent document identity
Multi-page section uses consistent margins and line spacing; bullets are indented and wrapped cleanly across lines
Subsection headings can appear near page transitions, indicating continuous flow across pages
Cross-references to appendices/notes are embedded inline and formatted as parenthetical or 'Refer to' statements
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines reporting period and scope using declarative statements
Uses quality-characteristic language: complete, neutral, accurate, free from material error, clear, and contextual
Explains estimation and judgement practices (inputs, assumptions, and transparency about forward-looking judgements)
States how commercially sensitive information is assessed before disclosure, without detailing the sensitive content
Positions the disclosures as intended to be read with general-purpose financial statements
Clarifies boundary alignment with financial reporting (same entities, policies, methods, estimates, and presentation currency) as a comparability mechanism
Signals first-time/voluntary adoption and describes incremental enhancement of controls/policies for future comparability
evidence_presentation_patterns: Uses references to authoritative standards and issuing bodies to ground the disclosure framework
Supports boundary and consistency claims by pointing to alignment with audited financial reporting constructs (policies/methods/estimates) rather than providing new evidence artifacts
Uses internal cross-references (notes/appendices/other reports) to direct readers to detailed supporting information
Flags when information extends beyond the primary reporting period for context and indicates that such instances are clearly identified
section_specific_observations: The section functions as a 'basis of preparation' and 'how to read this report' guide tailored to IFRS S1/S2
General requirements are operationalized through short, numbered subsections that mirror standard topics
Narrative alternates between principle statements (what the report aims to achieve) and mechanics (how boundaries, comparatives, and integration are handled)
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, brand references, or group/entity labels
Specific reporting year(s), dates, incorporation/merger history, legal citations, or jurisdictional commentary
Any mention of specific currencies, branch counts, geographic footprint, or business segment names
Any claims about being first/voluntary adopter framed as an achievement; keep only the abstract pattern of first-time adoption disclosure
Any references to specific note numbers, appendix identifiers, or proprietary report titles
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Reporting period and specific financial year references
References to specific jurisdictions/regions and endorsement status commentary
Legal incorporation/merger details and statutory law references
Business segment labels and descriptions of products/services
Geographic locations, branch counts, and subsidiary names
